chunks: And as for the right of the partner,

if he is absent, suffice him [in his affairs], and if he is present, show regard for him. Do not make a decision without his decision, and do not act on your own opinion without consulting him. Guard his property for him, and do not betray him in that which is difficult or of little importance of his affairs,
for God's hand is above the hands of the two partners as long as they do not betray each other. And there is no strength save in God.

key_terms.الشَّرِيكِ: Partner (in a business or joint venture)
key_terms.رَعَيْتَهُ: To show regard / care for him
key_terms.كَفَيْتَهُ: To suffice him / manage affairs on his behalf

ai.seo_question: What are the ethical obligations between business partners in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin expands the concept of partnership (sharik) beyond mere transaction to include spiritual fidelity, mandating that one partner acts as the guardian of the other's interests even in their absence. This narration underscores the principle of *mu'amara* (cohabitation/cooperation) in business, where mutual consultation and preservation of wealth are acts of worship, reflecting the divine presence in the bond between partners.

en.william-c-chittick: The right of the partner (sharik) is that

if he should be absent, you suffice him in his affairs, and if he should be present, you show regard for him. You make no decision without his decision and you do nothing on the basis of your own opinion, but you exchange views with him. You guard his property for him, and you do not betray him in that of his affair which is difficult or of little importance,
for God's hand is above the hands of two partners as long as they do not betray each other. And there is no strength save in God.
